answer: Each agent can be admitted only after posting a bond that is slashed if its signed actions are caught coordinating fraud, while rewards accrue gradually to identities with a history of useful, independently verified work. This makes a swarm of fresh aliases expensive: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it, then wait for each one to build reputation. A mesa of accounts cannot simply flow like a river around the rule; even a ferrous-sounding name earns no trust without costly proof over time.
